company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, also known as Stanford HAI, HAI, and AI Index, is a non-profit university lab founded in 2019 and headquartered in Stanford, CA, USA. Its website describes its mission as advancing humanity through AI and data science, with work focused on discovery, technological innovation, educational transformation, and societal impact. The institute describes human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout AI development and deployment. It says the combined institute retains the Stanford HAI name and is helmed by computer scientist James Landay, while co-founder Fei-Fei Li serves as Special Advisor on AI and joins John Hennessy as co-chair of the advisory council.

The site lists educational and research activities rather than commercial AI products. These include courses for leaders and decision-makers, specialized training for policymakers and civil servants, K-12 programs, grant programs, fellowships, and student affinity groups. It also highlights research on AI benchmarks, emergent agent behavior, AI privacy, and language digitization, with contributors including Surya Ganguli, Diyi Yang, Rob Reich, and Jennifer King. No products or MCP servers are listed for the institute.

The available data lists 281 California law exposure entries and no litigation cases. The institute is recorded as a non-profit university lab, not a for-profit company.
